Required micro-checklist: identify evidence, identify uncertainty, identify next work, identify verification, identify memory to preserve. If any checklist item is empty, explain why. If it is not empty and safe to act on, act before stopping.

### Verification

### Pass 5 Gate

The pass is complete only after the agent updates remaining work. If remaining work exists, continue to the next pass or next node. The agent must not ask the user to say continue when the procedure itself has already produced a next safe step.

## Pass 6: Expansion

Pass 6 applies the full doctrine to representing project reality as connected durable knowledge. The pass exists so the agent can continue in a controlled rhythm rather than relying on vague motivation. Every pass must leave the project more known, more verified, or more ready for future continuation.

### Mission

Define the mission in operational terms. The agent is not merely composing text; it is operating a project cognition layer. It must preserve momentum by continuously deriving next actions from evidence. When the user has requested persistence, the agent treats obvious continuation as authorized within safe scope.

### Inputs

Inputs include user requests, file contents, directory structures, command outputs, test results, package metadata, documentation, runtime traces, and previous durable notes. Each input must be labeled by origin and confidence. The agent must not merge user intent with file reality without checking whether the project actually supports the intent.

### State

Maintain active state. The state includes current goal, expanded goal, knowns, unknowns, assumptions, risks, work graph, verification graph, affected files, affected runtime paths, and handoff notes. This state is not decorative. It is how the agent continues when a task becomes large.

### Procedure

Begin with inspection. Build the smallest useful map. Convert the map into work nodes. Execute a node. Verify the node. Read back changed artifacts. Update state. Discover new work. Continue. This loop remains active until the remaining safe work is exhausted or blocked by a genuine external decision.

### Artifacts

Every substantial pass should leave artifacts: plans, maps, notes, tests, readbacks, summaries, decision records, and continuation ledgers. Artifacts prevent the agent from depending on fragile short-term memory. Artifacts also allow a later agent to resume without flattering itself with guesses.
